title: Customer Admin Guide — Build a Winning Proposal

lede: The complete customer manual: every feature of your proposal portal, in the order you use it — rank opportunities, build a content library, draft a proposal from your atoms in the canvas, lock the matrix, and export submission-ready files.
Every step was verified on a real effort: the Immobileyes NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS SBIR (topic DON26BX03-NP002). The screenshots are that live run.
hero.badge: Complete surface · every feature, screen, and control — verified on a live build

footer: govwin — RFP Pipeline Portal · Customer Admin role. Companion guides: RFP-Admin Operations, Collaborator.

sections.heading: Your portal — orientation
sections.lead: Welcome to your company’s proposal portal. This guide walks every feature you have as a Customer Admin, in the order you use them — from a ranked opportunity to a submission-ready, downloadable proposal. Sign in with the credentials your RFP-Pipeline admin issued; you land on your Dashboard.
sections.caption: The customer portal — your workspace, ToDos, and quick actions.

subs.heading: The sidebar & global chrome
subs.lead: The left sidebar is your map. It shows your company name, a notification bell, and your name up top; every workspace below.

callouts.html: The notification bell polls every 60s and badges unread (or 9+). If an RFP admin is working inside your company on your behalf, an amber shadow-admin banner shows at the top — everything they do is logged to your audit trail.

sections.heading: The Dashboard — home base
sections.lead: Your dashboard is role-aware: quick stats, your ToDo queue, an Add content dropzone, a getting-started checklist, and recent activity.

steps.t: Check the three stat cards (Library Units · Active Proposals · Pinned Topics) — each links to its screen.
Work Your To-Dos. Each card shows an urgency chip, a workflow pill, a step trail, and a typed action (Acknowledge / Approve-Done / Open-to-upload / a form).
steps.cap: The ToDo queue on your dashboard.

steps.t: Drop a file on Add content to upload & atomize it straight into your library.
Tick off the Get Started checklist (upload docs · set up profile · create a bucket · purchase a portal).
steps.cap: The getting-started checklist + recent activity.

callouts.html: A trial banner appears if your trial is ending — it turns red within 7 days and links to Billing so you keep your data.

sections.heading: Opportunities — your ranked pipeline
sections.lead: The Opportunity Pipeline is every opportunity the platform has released to you, ranked by your Spotlight buckets. Pin one to pull its documents into your workspace, then purchase a build.
sections.caption: The opportunity pipeline — ranked cards with pin, purchase, and build actions.

steps.t: Toggle Include closed to widen the list; Refresh re-pulls; the count shows how many cards you have.
Read a card: title, a submission-stage badge (NOFO / Pre-Release / Updated / Closed / Archived), agency, program type, and the close date.
steps.cap: A card’s stage badge and actions.

steps.t: Pin (copy docs) copies the solicitation’s documents into your workspace; a pinned card then shows Unpin and a green Purchase. Build → opens the build page. An Update available strip offers Resync when the RFP changes.

subs.heading: Purchasing a proposal workspace
subs.lead: The green Purchase button opens the purchase modal.
subs.caption: An opportunity’s detail view.

figures.cap: The card detail — Overview / Origin / Compliance tabs.

steps.t: The offer is a one-time expert-curated proposal build. Pay by card runs Stripe checkout, or use an Access / discount code.
Enter your comp code (e.g. rfppipelinetest) and Complete purchase. The build opens in curation_pending — an RFP admin then releases it (72h SLA), provisioning your matrix and molds.

callouts.html: In the verified run, the NAVAIR/NAVSEA C-UAS topic DON26BX03-NP002 ranked #1 for Immobileyes — the best fit for a counter-drone optics company.

sections.heading: Buckets — your scoring lenses
sections.lead: Spotlight buckets are your scoring criteria — the themes you care about. Each bucket ranks the whole pipeline by your rules, and editing one re-ranks your Opportunities automatically.
sections.caption: Spotlight buckets — define a lens, then rank the pipeline by it.

steps.t: In New bucket, set a Name plus any of keywords, agencies, program types, and NAICS codes; tick Include closed opportunities if you want them scored. Click Create.
steps.cap: Creating a scoring bucket.

steps.t: Click Rank → on a bucket to see your pipeline ordered #1, #2, … with each opportunity’s score and per-factor chips (e.g. keyword 3).
steps.cap: A bucket with its Rank control.

steps.t: Delete a bucket with its ✕. Ranking is deterministic today; an optional scoring agent overlays it later.

sections.heading: Library — build your content atoms
sections.lead: Your library is the raw material every draft is built from. You deconstruct your documents into tagged, sized atoms, then compose and reuse them. The page has three tabs — Library, Upload package, Atomize — plus a reuse-a-past-proposal panel.
sections.caption: The library — tagged atoms with grain, usage, lineage, and visibility.

subs.heading: Create a canvas · start from a template · downloads
subs.lead: Beyond hand-shredding, you can create a canvas — a foundation artifact (a whole doc / deck / sheet / PDF) that decomposes on save into reusable section / group / atom grains — and copy in ready-made starter templates.

steps.t: Click Create canvas. The Blank tab mints a foundation from a form (Document · Deck · Sheet · PDF) with a kind × context taxonomy, and opens straight in the canvas editor.
steps.cap: Create canvas — a blank foundation by form + taxonomy.

steps.t: The Start from a template tab lists the shared starter catalog — capability statement, one-pager, SBIR/STTR technical & cost volumes, DoW CSO brief, commercialization deck. Use copies one into your library as your own editable canvas (with lineage back to the original).
steps.cap: Start from a template — the starter catalog, copy-on-use.

steps.t: When your library is empty, the starter offer appears at the top — Add all N bulk-copies the whole starter set in one click (idempotent; addable anytime).
steps.cap: The starter-set offer on an empty library.

steps.t: Browse library filters foundations / sections / groups / atoms by kind × form × context × vehicle (facet counts update live), and every row offers a native-format download (.docx · .pptx · .xlsx · .pdf).
steps.cap: The faceted library browser with per-row downloads.

callouts.html: Collaboration vaults (nooks) — a customer-owned, RLS-segregated branch library per external partner — are provisioned server-side (create · invite · upload/atomize · download-whole · ingest, with the isolation contract adversarially proven). The two-sided nook UI ships next.

steps.t: Filter with the search box, the grain select (primitive / group / foundational), the status select, and a My atoms / All atoms toggle. Click a tag chip to filter by it.
steps.cap: The library filter bar.

steps.t: Select atoms with their checkboxes to reveal the bulk bar: Approve all, Archive all, and a tag-dimension + value → Tag all.
steps.cap: The bulk / compose bar appears on selection.

steps.t: With two or more selected, name the group (e.g. “Team for Navy”) and Group into new atom to compose a reusable bundle.
steps.cap: Composing primitives into a group.

steps.t: Click an atom title to open its detail drawer — confirmed vs unconfirmed tags, lineage (↖ derived from / ↳ reused in), and a content preview.
steps.cap: Real library atoms — grain, tags, usage, source badges, and lineage.

table.title: Atom vocabulary
rows: primitive (one block) · group (a bundle) · foundational (a whole reference doc)
uploaded · returned (harvested back from a locked section)

subs.heading: Upload a package (bulk atomize)
subs.lead: The fastest way to fill the library: drop a whole proposal package and let the atomizer shred it.

steps.t: On Upload package, drop up to 12 files (PDF·DOCX·PPTX·XLSX·TXT·MD) or Choose files.
steps.cap: The upload-package control.

steps.t: Add optional Package context (name, agency, program, phase, solicitation, topic) — it’s stamped on every atom minted from the package.
Click Atomize package. Each file becomes a reference atom plus one primitive per substantive block, auto-tagged against the taxonomy.

callouts.html: Verified: five Immobileyes documents atomized into 24 atoms — tagged vol:technical vol:cost vol:key_personnel kind:bio and more.

figures.cap: The real atomizer — 24 tagged atoms from five documents.

subs.heading: Atomize — the hand-shredder
subs.lead: The Atomize tab is precision control: paste or upload a document, and box exactly what becomes an atom.

steps.t: Paste text (a bio, a past-performance blurb, a whole team section) and Deconstruct, or upload a file. The document becomes a list of typed objects (figure / table / list / heading / text).
Set the Session context (the “FROM” pedigree — agency, program, phase, solicitation, topic) so everything minted this session inherits it.
Select an object, give it a title, add curated + free tags, and Make atom (or Make group for a table/list). Minted atoms collect in the Section tray.
Select several tray items, name it, and Box section to wrap them into a section group.

subs.heading: Reuse a past proposal (templify)
subs.body: At the top of the page, Reuse a past proposal lists your uploaded proposals. Save as template extracts a proposal’s structure into a reusable skeleton (pick a template type → Extract structure); once templated, New draft spins up a fresh document from that skeleton. This is how a winning structure becomes the starting point for the next bid.

subs.heading: Capture from screen (box → tag → atomize)
subs.lead: The Capture tab pulls content from anywhere on your screen — a Google Doc, a data sheet, a web page — without connecting an account. It’s the box-and-tag Atomize flow applied to a screenshot.
subs.caption: The Capture tab — grab from any window/tab/screen, one-way in.

steps.t: Click ▣ Capture from screen and pick a window, tab, or screen. The frame freezes on the canvas and the screen-share stops immediately — no lingering access.
Drag boxes over the parts worth keeping. Give each region a title and tag it with the same vocabulary as the Atomize tab (vol kind fmt …); add a source URL + note for provenance.

Optionally name a section to group the regions, then Atomize N region(s) → library. Each region becomes a draft image atom (anchored to a reference of the whole frame), ready to review and insert into a section canvas.

callouts.html: One-way by design: only the crops you send ever leave your screen — the platform never receives your Google/social credentials and holds no connection back to the source. Captures land as draft atoms with a “Screen capture from <host> · <time>” provenance stamp.
Verified end-to-end: a captured frame boxed into two regions produced a reference atom + two tagged region atoms + a section group — all draft, provenance-stamped, insertable into the canvas.

sections.heading: Proposals — your builds
sections.lead: Every proposal for your company. Proposals aren’t created here — they appear when you purchase a topic and an RFP admin releases it.
sections.caption: The proposals list — each row opens its build workspace.

steps.t: Each row shows the title, agency, topic, section count, created date, a due/closed date (red if overdue), and a stage pill in the customer V0.5 → V1 labels.
Click a row to open its build workspace (the compliance matrix).
steps.cap: A proposal row — stage pill, section count, and dates.

sections.heading: The proposal workspace & compliance matrix
sections.lead: Opening a proposal gives you the build cockpit: a stage-control bar, the volume/section matrix, team & access, compliance, AI, and export. As an admin you get the full admin panel (four tabs).
sections.caption: The proposal workspace — 6-volume matrix, ready to draft and lock.

steps.t: The bar shows stage progress dots for each gate (done ✓ / current / future), the due date, and a gate-requirements button (N requirement(s) pending or All gates met ✓).
The primary action is Advance to {next} →; at Final you get Unlock for Edit / Re-lock. If an advance is blocked, an amber list names the unlocked sections (admins can Force advance anyway →).

callouts.html: After two proposal locks, further changes require RFP-Pipeline support — the bar says so. Downloads unlock once the proposal is locked/submitted.

subs.heading: The admin panel — 4 tabs
subs.lead: The admin panel is your build console.

table.title: Admin-panel tabs
rows: volume groups with per-section Accept & Lock, page-fill gauges, Lock Volume, Download (docx) / PDF, Accept & Lock All, and the whole-proposal export row
the TeamManager — invite collaborators, per-section grants, the E/C/V access matrix
Run Compliance Check (AI), the compliance checklist, and stage-gate requirements
Draft with AI across empty sections, and Record Outcome (Won/Lost/Withdrawn)

steps.t: In Artifacts, each section row shows a status pill, assignee, a page-fill bar, and Accept & Lock (→ 🔒 Unlock). When every section in a volume is locked, the volume reads ✓ Volume locked and the Download + PDF links light up.
steps.cap: A volume group with its lock + download controls.

steps.t: The export row — Download Proposal (.docx) and Download all (.zip) — enables once the proposal is locked.
steps.cap: The proposal export controls.

figures.cap: The live matrix — volumes with per-section Accept & Lock, status pills, and Volume-locked downloads.

subs.heading: Compliance, team & AI tabs
subs.lead: The other three admin-panel tabs run your review, your people, and your AI.

steps.t: Compliance tab — Run Compliance Check fires an AI pass that scores your proposal against the solicitation’s requirements (pass/fail/partial per variable). Below it, the Compliance Checklist and the Stage Gate Requirements (add a gate with a stage + label, toggle each met).
Team & Access tab — the TeamManager: + Invite a collaborator (email, name, role, permission, and the sections to assign), then read the Access Matrix (sections × people, E/C/V cells).

AI & Library tab — Draft with AI queues a draft for every empty section; Record Outcome (Won/Lost/Withdrawn, once submitted) feeds the result back into your library so winning content ranks higher next time.

callouts.html: Invite grants are per section and per permission (view / comment / edit). A collaborator only ever sees the sections you assign — see the Collaborator guide for the full picture.
AI & Library also hosts Research this opportunity — the R&D scout (see 7.5).

subs.heading: Research this opportunity (R&D scout)
subs.lead: In the AI & Library tab, the Research Scout does your R&D — market research, prior art, and the competitor landscape, including DoD sources (SAM.gov, SBIR.gov, DSIP) — and returns a cited brief.
subs.caption: Research this opportunity — the R&D scout, in the AI & Library tab.

steps.t: Type (or refine) the research question, then click 🔎 Research this opportunity. The scout runs in the background: it browses the web through a controlled server-side browser, then synthesizes the findings.

When it finishes, the cited brief appears inline — findings with [source] links and confidence, plus the competitor list. It’s advisory: review it and pull the useful bits into your Library / sections; it never changes your proposal by itself.

callouts.html: Safe by design: every page the scout reads is treated as untrusted data (never instructions), the run is budget/rate-capped (usage shows in AI Usage), and it safe-skips — returning no sources rather than inventing them — if web access is unavailable. Use more, get more.

subs.heading: Opportunity origin & compliance
subs.body: The collapsible Opportunity origin & compliance card has three tabs — Overview (build stage, lock count, deadlines), Origin (frozen-at-purchase: opportunity, agency, program, topic #, solicitation #, bought-from bucket), and Compliance (a live “{x}/{y} mandatory satisfied — {pct}%” bar and a Satisfied / Partial / Not-addressed / N-A grid). It’s your at-a-glance readiness read.

sections.heading: The section canvas — where you write
sections.lead: The canvas is the WYSIWYG editor for one section — what you see is what exports. Open a section from the matrix. The top bar carries the title, a status pill, export buttons, Undo/Redo, + From Library, Save, and (admins) Complete & Lock.
sections.caption: The canvas editor — toolbar, page canvas, and the toolbox sidebar.

steps.t: The INSERT group adds a block after the selected one; the FORMAT group (B / I / align / size / color) acts on the selected text block.
steps.cap: The canvas formatting toolbar.

steps.t: Click any node to edit it in place; drag the handle to reorder. Each node type has its own inline editor.

table.title: Canvas node types
rows: textarea + B / I / U / superscript / subscript mini-toolbar
click-to-upload, alt text, caption, size, replace

subs.heading: The toolbox sidebar
subs.lead: The sidebar opens on Your toolbox — a prioritized card list resolved from your role and the stage — then offers tabs.

table.title: Sidebar tabs
rows: document status, a real word-budget gauge (“{words}/{max} words · N-page limit”), fonts/margins, content-source dots (AI / library / manual)
the selected block’s provenance + actions (Move, Accept, Revert, Delete, Replace from Library), a full Format panel, per-node History, Comments, and an AI Revision panel
a 12-button grid of every node type
“Review · Modify · Lock” — admins get Complete & Lock this section; others save for an admin to lock
the version list (AI Draft / Human Edit / Library / …) — click any to preview
the floorplan — margins, fonts, line spacing, page/slide limit, header/footer templates

figures.cap: The Compliance tab — live word-budget gauge, fonts, and content-source dots.

steps.t: Click Draft (or Draft all sections from the admin panel). The drafting agent reads the RFP context and the section’s mold, pulls the most relevant atoms, and writes canvas content sized to the page budget.

On a text node, open AI Revision for one-click rewrites: Regenerate · Make shorter · Make longer · More specific · Simpler language · Stronger opening · Add metrics · Fix compliance, or a custom instruction.

callouts.html: Verified: the proposal.draft_section agent ran on all 8 Technical-Volume sections, grounded in the atomized library, to a ~1,090-word / 2-page target per section. Nothing auto-commits — it’s advisory until you accept.

steps.t: + From Library opens the insert panel: it ranks your atoms for this section (with “✦ N context match(es)”). Tick atoms and Insert N atom(s) into the canvas — they become section nodes.
steps.cap: The insert-from-library panel ranks your atoms for this section.

steps.t: The picked atoms flow straight into the canvas as editable nodes.
steps.cap: Atoms inserted into the section canvas.

steps.t: On a selected node, Replace from Library swaps its content for a better-matching atom (sortable by best-match / most-used / most-recent).
Drag nodes to reorder them into the flow you want.
steps.cap: Reordering nodes on the canvas.

subs.heading: Harvest back to the library
subs.body: The Library (N) button opens the atomize rail — each library-eligible node becomes a bubble you can classify (choose a type), tag, and Accept as atom, harvesting your best content back into the library for reuse. Accept all does the batch.

steps.t: When a section is right, Complete & Lock (top bar or the Review tab). Locking flips its compliance row to satisfied, snapshots the version, and harvests reusable content back to your library.
steps.cap: The Accept & Lock control.

steps.t: Locked sections are read-only; Unlock reopens one for edits (admins).

callouts.html: Verified: locking turned 10 matrix rows green (8 Technical + 2 Cost); Volume 2 read “8/8 locked · 9/10 pages · ✓ Volume locked.”

subs.heading: The slide editor
subs.lead: When the artifact is a slide deck, the same shell becomes the SlideEditor.

steps.t: The left Slides panel is your thumbnail navigator — each thumb shows the slide title and element count; + Add Slide appends one (you can’t delete the last).
Edit the active slide with the embedded canvas (16:9 or 4:3). The info bar reads “Slide N of M · N element(s).” Export the deck with Export .pptx from the top bar.

subs.heading: The spreadsheet editor
subs.lead: A spreadsheet artifact (like a Cost Volume) opens the SheetEditor — a real grid with formulas.

figures.cap: The spreadsheet editor — a cost section with live formulas.

steps.t: Use the cell-reference box (e.g. A1) and the formula bar (fx) to enter values and formulas; the format bar handles bold, alignment, fill color, size, and font.
Add rows/columns with the trailing + controls; manage multiple sheet tabs at the bottom (double-click to rename). Export .xlsx writes the workbook with formulas intact.

callouts.html: Verified: the Cost Volume exported to a submission-ready .xlsx with live formulas — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k.

sections.heading: Compliance Review — the readiness check
sections.lead: A read-only readiness view across sections and the compliance matrix.
sections.body: The top banner reads Ready for Final Submission (green) or Not Ready — Items Need Attention (amber), with a stats bar (Sections Locked · Requirements Met · Est. Pages · Stage). Below, a Section Status table (with page estimates and “(over)” flags) and a Compliance Checklist (each requirement’s status, source, and notes). Use it as your pre-submit gate.

sections.heading: Documents — everything in one place
sections.lead: Every document across the workspace, in five tables: your standalone documents, proposal sections, supporting documents, library uploads, and solicitation source documents.
sections.caption: The documents hub — five tables covering every file type.

steps.t: + New Document starts a standalone canvas document; Upload Document sends a file to the library.
In Supporting Documents, use the per-row actions: Upload (presigned), Download, and admin Review / Approve / Waive to advance a required attachment’s status.
steps.cap: The documents hub — standalone docs, proposal sections, and supporting files.

subs.heading: New document chooser
subs.caption: The new-document chooser — blank presets or a template.
subs.body: Start blank offers four presets — One-page flier, Blank document, Slide deck, Workbook. Start from a template filters your templates and the system library; each card previews the structure and Use template opens the editor. A standalone document has its own Lock for download bar.

sections.heading: Activity & Processes — audit and automation

figures.cap: The activity stream — filterable audit timeline.

sections.body: Activity is your audit timeline — namespace tabs (All/Proposal/Library/…), a type search, time ranges, auto-refresh, and expandable event payloads. Processes lists your running automations with health chips (Failing/Stalled/Awaiting input/Running/Done); admins can Move to next gate on a paused step and expand the Steps timeline.

sections.heading: Team — members & collaborators
sections.caption: The team page — members, roles, and proposal collaborators.

steps.t: Invite a member with Email, Name, and Role (Contributor / Admin / External Partner).
steps.cap: The invite control.

steps.t: The Team Members table lets admins Deactivate / Reactivate a member (never hard-deleted). Proposal Collaborators lists per-proposal partners and their accepted/pending status.

subs.heading: Automation preferences

figures.cap: Automation preferences — toggle what runs automatically.

subs.body: Automation (admins) toggles notifications (document ready · collaborator get-ready · stage advanced · new priority opportunity), AI (review on advance), and flow (auto-advance when all locked). Save to apply.

subs.heading: Company profile

figures.cap: Settings — your company profile feeds AI drafting.

subs.body: Settings shows your account + subscription and the editable Company Profile (legal name, website, summary, technology focus, NAICS, set-asides, target agencies, keywords). These fields feed proposal templates and AI drafting, so keep them current.

subs.heading: Billing & Builds & AI Usage
subs.body: Billing manages your Spotlight subscription, expert-consulting hours, and purchase history. Builds (/portals) lists your purchased proposal portals with their lifecycle status (curation_pending shows the 72h SLA countdown; launched/executing offer stage controls). AI Usage (/agents) shows your agent calls, allocation used, per-agent breakdown, and recent activity.

sections.heading: Export — your submission-ready files
sections.lead: With a volume locked, download your deliverables. The Technical Volume exports to a submission-ready .docx (US-Letter, 1″ margins, the agency’s fonts, figures inline & captioned); the Cost Volume to an .xlsx with live formulas.
sections.caption: Page 1 of the exported Technical Volume — rendered by the system from your locked canvas.

callouts.html: Verified deliverables: a 10-page Technical Volume .docx (6 figures, 5 tables, 8 DON TV2 sections) and a Cost Volume .xlsx — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k, formulas live.
